speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for telling me about your dizziness and vertigo episodes. To help me understand your condition better, can you describe the specific nature of these spells—do they feel like the room is spinning, or is it more of a lightheaded feeling? Also, do these episodes get triggered by specific movements or positions?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your episodes are position-dependent, do you experience them specifically when rolling over in bed, looking up, or bending down? Additionally, how long does each episode of spinning typically last?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
